scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Unitarizability implies amenability for discrete groups” (preprints/Unitarizability-Implies-Amenability-for-Countable-Groups-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 251 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 deec58813ffe560e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: A discrete group is amenable if and only if it is unitarizable. For every discrete nonamenable group G and every ε > 0, there are a complex Hilbert space K and a representation π : G → GL(K) with |π| ≤ 1 + ε that is not similar to a unitary representation. If G is countable, K may be chosen separable.
